req: Particles in the water must read as flowing water, not as bubbles or white balls.
check: look head: tracers are streaks along the bore. Root cause was `mats.fleck` missing from the unit's material table, so Three fell back to a white MeshBasicMaterial.

req: Colours must NEVER change suddenly; every change is a gradient.
check: One recipe everywhere, and since F13 the recipe's input is a temperature: colourOfT(T) is the only place a colour is made, and every paint call reads a leg's T0/T1. Any new call site that mixes its own colour breaks this, hence WATCH.

proof.caption: Sea water warming across the tube bank

req: The condensate is the same temperature as the water going back to the boiler, so it must be the same colour, and the tank below the turbine must look full of water, not painted walls.
check: look sump: pool and suction line painted from one call. Measured on the current build: pool body (76,96,139), suction line (74,90,133), within 3% per channel.

proof.caption: Condensate pool and its suction line

req: Water must visibly become more orangish towards the top of the reactor, realistically, not paint in front.
check: look rpv: vertical ramp on the body of the water, cold at the bottom of the vessel to amber at the surface.

proof.caption: Reactor: blue at the bottom, amber at the top

req: Steam speed in the pipe must be consistent with the steam in the boiler; fluid speeds consistent overall.
check: One compression law drawV(v) = 2.6 * |v|^0.55 drives every scroll, tracer, riser and vapour cloud.

proof.text: js/view/unit.js: drawV() is the only speed mapping; grep -n 'drawV(' shows every scroll and tracer uses it.

req: Junctions between pipe and vessel must be seamless: no colour step, no grey rod, no sleeve, no 'dark orange pipe and light orange tank'.
check: look head: hot and cold legs run to the divider plate inside the head; all ten collars deleted; one colour call per junction.

proof.caption: Hot and cold legs entering the channel head

req: The incoming water pipe must be seamless and properly connected to the rest.
check: look dome: the feed line runs through the shell and ends inside the vessel at the head of the downcomer; the downcomer sheet now starts exactly where the pipe stops and runs to the tube sheet whatever the water level, so the arriving water is seen to run down it. There is no ring.

req: The blue pipe into the boiler must look like fluid going into a bigger tank.
check: look dome.

req: Water must be rendered the way games and physical simulations render fluids: a clean, standard model, not a hack. 'No game would ship such poor graphics.'
check: Standard real-time water model: two-octave flow map (aperiodic FBM, anisotropic along the bore), Beer-Lambert absorption by path length, Fresnel edge, glossy specular; refraction available as a toggle. Marked WATCH because the bar is 'game quality' and reflections of surroundings are still off by default for frame rate.

req: If sea water is heated by condensing the steam, the pipe after the turbine must look orangish, less than the reactor.
check: Leg 'sea water' picks up 10 C across the condenser (dT), drawn with a display gain of 10 so the change is visible: outfall at 115 C on the map, against 317 C for water off the fuel. Measured: outfall line (141,93,65), warm; intake (66,94,150), blue.

req: The INCOMING sea water is colder than the outgoing water and must be blue, not orange.
check: The sea leg's inlet temperature is the sea's, 15 C, and the intake pipe carries the leg's inlet end (tempAt 'in'); the first tube pass flows against its geometry and says so with flowDir. Measured: intake tube (66,94,150), blue.

proof.caption: Intake blue where the sea arrives

req: The sea must look like one seamless surface, no patches with different textures.
check: Open sea, forebay and channel set their ripple repeat from SEA_TILE and share the two-octave flow. WATCH: at the bay camera the forebay still reads flatter than the open water beside it; the boundary itself needs its own shot before this is called done.

check: 28 buttresses removed; steam and feed leave the containment in one corner.

req: No em dashes in interface copy.
check: grep over index.html, js/ui.js, js/view/labels.js, js/scenarios.js returns nothing.

proof.text: grep -rn '\u2014' index.html js/ui.js js/view/labels.js js/scenarios.js -> no matches

req: Use a proper engine for the fluids: design the 3-D structures, put water in them, set the sea's temperature and say where heat goes in, and let the engine derive the colours. No hand-assigned colours per pipe.
check: Temperature travels with the water: every Leg in js/flow.js carries T0/T1/dT and Circuit.setTemps walks the chain in flow order. unit.js solveTemps() sets ONE inlet temperature per circuit and the dT of the legs that exchange heat (core, boiler tubes, condenser bank, pool coil). colourOfT() is the only place a temperature becomes a colour. grep 'fluidColour(' in unit.js: only colourOfT calls it. Measured on this build: intake tube (66,94,150), outfall line (141,93,65): the sea leg enters at 15 C and leaves at 15 + 10 x gain 10 = 115 C, and nothing was told a colour.

proof.caption: Sea leg: in at 15 C, out warmer, colours derived
Primary loop: cold leg to hot leg from the core's rise

req: With Refraction switched on the liquids must not go near black.
check: stage.setQuality('refraction'): the fluid shader's absorption density steps back to a quarter while transmission is on, and is restored when it is off.

req: Bloom must not cost most of the frame rate.
check: Bloom is off by default on every device and, on, runs on a buffer 0.34 of the frame on each axis (a ninth of the pixels) instead of 0.6. Measured at 1200x800 on this build: bloom off 10.6 ms a frame, bloom on 10.2 ms; the difference is inside the noise.

proof.text: js/view/stage.js: bloom default false; setSize(w*0.34, h*0.34). Measured: 10.6 ms off, 10.2 ms on.

req: In the tsunami the flood must cover the emergency water tank and the pump beside it; when the text says the sea has receded, the water must be gone.
check: The flood sheet reaches into the section (its hole round the containment is gone: this model keeps the equipment a tsunami drowns inside the cutaway), rises at 2.5 m/s, is painted as sea water, and a 14 m wave puts about five metres on the deck (clamp((flooded-5.7)*0.9, 0, 7.6)). The recede event sets flooded back to 0.8 and the sheet drops.

proof.caption: Tsunami at 55 min, from outside: the emergency tank and its pump are under the water

check: The breach plume is released 4.5 m outside the wall with a 2.2 m spread and rises; the tear is a ragged rim of flat concrete shards set into the wall round the opening.
